newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares set for further rises.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares set for further rises.

text.p: The Brussels blue-chip Bel-20 index kept in positive territory on Wednesday, helped by rises in the U.S. market, with dealers expecting the index to touch the psychological 2,100 level within days.
"Next week we're likely to see the 2,100 level," said trader Paul de Lophem at brokerage Mignon, Hanart, Declerck.
He added that the market would be helped by derivative products which banks would be launching until March 15.
The blue-chip Bel-20 closed up 0.32 percent at 2,087.63, after earlier touching an all-time intraday high of 2,096.38.
Retailer Delhaize was the Bel-20's main gainer, helped by the bullish dollar, up 2.26 percent at 2,035 francs with over 263 million Belgian francs worth of the share traded.
"Delhaize has been fairly good today following the rise in Food Lion," said Paul de Lophem.
JP Morgan said on Wednesday it initiated coverage of Food Lion Inc with a market performer rating. Food Lion is a unit of Belgian Delhaize.
Chemical firm Tessenderlo jumped 3.1 percent to 15,850 francs.
"Investors have been switching from Solvay to buy Tessenderlo," said analyst and trader Gert De Mesure at Bank Delen.

Chemical firm Solvay fell 2.1 percent to 21,000 francs, after earlier having lost over three percent, as investors continued to dump the stock after last week's lower-than-expected preliminary 1996 profits.
"People are still switching out of the stock, with three of its five divisions in a difficult environment, but investors are hoping that the pharmaceutical sector will show results," De Mesure said.

Elsewhere shares in Fortis AG, the Belgian arm of Belgo-Dutch financial group Fortis, fell 1.71 percent to 5,760 francs as investors saw news of the subscription price for its capital increase as an opportunity to take profits.
"There is some arbitrage between the share price and people buying at the subscription price," said De Mesure.
Another share which saw profit-taking was retailer Colruyt, falling 0.98 percent to 15,175 francs, with dealers putting it down to a correction from recent rises.
